title: Software
text: I contribute to open-source statistical software for multilevel modeling and effect size estimation in single-case experimental designs.

title: Software
text:
lmeInfo
R package
Tools for computing analytic derivatives and information matrices for linear mixed-effects and generalized least squares models fitted with nlme. The package supports inference for variance components and estimation of design-comparable standardized mean differences.
Coauthors: James E. Pustejovsky and Man Chen.

 Documentation  CRAN  GitHub

title: Software
text:
scdhlm
R package and web application
Tools for estimating hierarchical linear models and between-case standardized mean differences from single-case designs. These effect sizes support comparisons with results from between-subjects randomized experiments. The package accommodates treatment reversal, multiple baseline, and multiple probe designs, including more complex multilevel structures.
The accompanying web application provides an interactive calculator for between-case standardized mean differences.
Package coauthors: James E. Pustejovsky, Man Chen, and Bethany H. Bhat.
Web application coauthors: James E. Pustejovsky, Man Chen, Bethany H. Bhat, and Paulina Grekov.

 Documentation  CRAN  GitHub  Open web app

title: Software
text:
SingleCaseES
R package and web application
A toolkit for calculating effect sizes for single-case designs, including non-overlap measures, within-case standardized mean differences, and response ratios. Standard errors and confidence intervals are available for measures with known sampling distributions.
The single-case effect size calculator offers an interactive interface to these measures. The project documentation recommends the hosted app for demonstrations; for research, install the R package and run its interface locally in RStudio.
Package and web application coauthors: James E. Pustejovsky, Man Chen, Paulina Grekov, and Daniel M. Swan.

 Documentation  CRAN  GitHub  Open web app

title: Publications and Preprints
text: My research focuses on developing and evaluating statistical methods to address methodological challenges that arise when applying meta-analytic techniques to real-world datasets, including dependent effect sizes, selective reporting and publication bias, and design-comparable effect sizes. I am also interested in statistical methods for single-case experimental designs.

title: Man Chen
text:
I am a quantitative methodologist and assistant professor in the Department of Educational Psychology at University of Texas at Austin.
My research focuses on developing and evaluating statistical methods to address scientific questions in education and psychology. I am particularly interested in solving methodological challenges that arise when applying meta-analytic techniques to real-world datasets, including dependent effect sizes, selective reporting and publication bias, and design-comparable effect sizes.

title: Teaching
text: I teach graduate courses in quantitative methods in the Department of Educational Psychology at The University of Texas at Austin. These courses connect statistical concepts with practical data analysis and programming in R.

title: Teaching
text:
Hierarchical Linear Modeling
An introduction to multilevel models for nested and longitudinal data, such as students within schools and repeated measurements within individuals. Topics include random intercept and random slope models, longitudinal models, and multilevel generalized linear models. Students learn to select and fit appropriate models, interpret results, and communicate findings, with demonstrations in R.

 Fall 2026 syllabus  Fall 2025 syllabus  Fall 2024 syllabus

title: Teaching
text:
Correlation and Regression Methods
A foundation in the theory and application of correlation and regression methods. Students learn to specify, conduct, and interpret correlation analyses and regression models. Analyses and computing demonstrations use R.

title: Teaching
section: Statistical Modeling and Simulation in R
text:
Statistical Modeling and Simulation in R
An advanced R course focuses on designing and implementing Monte Carlo simulation studies for methodological research (e.g., evaluating statistical methods) and empirical applications (e.g., conducting power analysis), debugging, functional and object-oriented programming, and an introduction to R package and Shiny app development with GitHub integration.
